FatalAccidents on National Highways 
*342. PROF. A. LAKSHMISAGAR: 
SHRI H.K. JAVARE GOWDA: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS bepleasedto 
state: 
(a) whether Government have made any assessment of the fatal road 
accidents on the country's highways a nd the percentage by which such 
accidents have risen during the last three years; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, year-wise; 
(c) whether Government have critically evaluated the factors responsible 
for the rising number of such fatal road accidents besides examining the highways 
designs; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the measures contemplated by Government to make the National 
Highways more safe ? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT 
AND HIGHWAYS [(MAJ. GEN. (RETD.) B.C. KHANDUPJ)]: (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. 
The data on road accidents on the Na tional Highways are collected annually 
from the States. As per information available, for the years 1998, 1999 and 2000 
the percentage rise in number of fatalities on National Highways each year has 
been about 3.2%. 4.5%and 3.8% respectively. The data for years 1998,1999 and 
2000 are provisional and as such percentage increase are also provisional. 
(c) and (d) analysis of the various road accidents attributes the causes of 
road accidents to drivers, pedestrians/passengers, mechanical defects in motor 
vehicles, bad weather, condition of roads and other causes. 
(e) Necessary measures of road Sa fety on all National Highways are 
incorporated in the Road Design at the detailed project report stage for the 
concerned National Highways. The Government is taking a number of steps 
besides highway design to improve the road safety on National Highways. 
These include: 
(i) Giving grant-in-aid to voluntary organizations for administering 
road safety programmes in order to create awareness among the 
public. 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [13 December. 2001] 
(ii) Refresher training of Heavy Motor Vehicle Drivers and use of 
driving'simulators. 
(iii) Publicity campaign on Road Safety Awareness through audio-
visual-print media. 
(iv) National Award has been instituted for voluntary organizations/ 
individuals for outstanding work in the field of road safety. 
(v) All India Essay Competition on road safety are organizaed for 
school children for creating awareness among the school children. 
(vi) Observance of Road Safety Week in the first week of every year 
across the country. 
(vii) Annual fitness certificate of commercial vehicles is necessary as 
per provision of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. 
(viii) Introduction of Smart Card, based driving licenses. 
(ix) Transport Minister's Trophy for State Transport Undertakings 
having lowest accident record, etc. 
(x) Provision of cranes and ambulances under National Highway 
Accident Relief Service Scheme to States/NGOs, etc. 
(xi) Road Patrolling on a part of National Highways-8 has been taken 
up as an experimental measure. 
Labour Reforms 
*343. SHRI SURESH PA CHOURI: Will the Minist er of LABOUR be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to introduce labour reforms in the country; 
(b) if so, the details; and 
(c) the reasons for delay in introducin g labour reforms in the wake of 
introduction of structural reforms since 1991 ? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR (SHRI SHARAD YADAV) : (a) to (c) 
Review/updation of labour laws is a continuous process in order to bring them 
in tune with the prevailing situation and emerging needs of the economy. Taking 
into consideration the requirement of productivity, competitiveness and 
employment generation and to update the provisions, especially since the 
introduction of economic reforms beginning 1991. need has been felt from time

lo time to make amendments in certain labour legislations and steps initiated

Central Assistance to States 
*347. SHRI KRISHNA KUMAR BIRL A: 
SHRI AN ANTRA Y DEVSHANKER DAVE:  
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Planning Commission have decided to review the 
Gadgil-Mukherjee formula for allocation of Central Assistance to States; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether several Slates are unhappy on the allocation of Central 
Assistance due to Gadgil-Mukherjee formula; and 
(d) if so, the details of representations received in this regard and further 
action taken thereon ? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRTMATIVASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) to (d) The Planning Commission has 
received proposals from various State Governments to amend the existing Gadgil 
formula for allocating Normal Central Assistance to State Plans. There is wide 
divergence in the views amongst the States in this regard- In general, while the 
advanced States have sought higher weightage for performance, the less 
advanced States have sought higher weightage for backwardness. This issue

Development Council (NDC), it was decided that given the difference of opinion 
among the State Governments and the sensitivity of this issue, it was necessary 
to discuss this further and evolve a consensus before alternatives are considered 
by the NDC. 
Ceiling on bonus 
*348. SHRI JIBON ROY : Will the Minister of LABOUR be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that upper ceiling of the guaranteed bonus for the 
industrial workers has not been changed since last decades; 
(b) the details of the upper ceiling stipulated when the Bonus Act was 
passed with corresponding Consumer Price Index and the current upper ceiling 
with the corresponding Consumer Price Index; and 
7 

RAJYASABHA [13 December,2001] 
(c) the steps taken by Government to withdraw upper ceiling on payment 
of bonus ? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR (SHRISHARAD YAD AV) : (a) to (c) The 
Payment of Bonus Act was enacted in 1965. Originally the Act provided for an 
eligibility limit of Rs. 1600 p.m. of wages and calculation ceiling of Rs. 750 p.m. 
which were raised to Rs. 2500 and Rs. 1600 respectively in 1985 (w.e.f. 7-11-85). 
The ceilings were subsequently raised to Rs. 3500 and Rs. 2500 respectively in 
1995, effective 1 -4-93. The Consumer Price Index Numbers for Industrial Workers 
(base 1960 = 100) for the year 1965 was 132 and for 1985, it was 625. The index as 
on 1 -4-93 with new CPI base (1982) was 243 which when converted to 1960 base 
comes to 1198. The latest CPI at 1982 base is 468 for the month of October, 2001 
which works out to 2307 at 1960 base. 
The Government is seized of the demand regarding the amendment of 
Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 for raising the eligibility and calculation ceilings. 
The issue is under examination in the light of its wide ranging repercussions as 
the benefits of bonus will have to be extended to, besides the Private Sector, to 
the employees of PSUs (both Central and States), Central and State Governments 
and autonomous organizations resulting in huge financial burden to the 
Government exchequer.

Indian in foreign jails 
*352. SHR1 NANA DESHMUKH : Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the nevs-item 
captioned "In foreign jails Indian are bound in red tape" appearing in the 
'Hindustan times' dated the 8th November, 2001; 
(b) whether the families of Indian prisoners, who are more than 6,600, in 
foreign jails have applied through his Ministry for release of their wards; and 
(c) if so, the cases in which his Ministry has helped their early release ? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRIJ AS WANT SINGH) : 
(a) Yes, Sir, the Government has noted the news itern^ 
(b) From time to time the Government receives requests for assistance for 
the release of Indian prisoners, from foreign jails, from their families and others. 
(c) As soon as Indian diplomatic mission is informed of the arrest of an 
Indian citizen in a foreign country, a request is hiade by it to the host Government, 
for seeking consular access. An official of the Mission visits the detainee to 
ascertain the circumstances leading to the arrest. Where necessary the Mission 
takes up the matter with the host Government for speedy and fair trial and also 
for review of the sentence. The prisoners are normally released on completion of 
their sentences. In deserving cases, our Missions approach the local authorities 
for remission of sentences. 
In Gulf countries, during the holy month of ramadan our Missions send 
formal requests for Royal Pardon for release of Indian prisoners on humanitarian 
grounds. 
The arrest and release of indian prisoners abroad is a continuous process.
